To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) a novel inductive co-training framework for semi-supervised multi-lable learning is proposed and 2) it performs favorably against other state-of-the-art approaches.
We propose a novel semi-supervised multi-lable learning algorithm COINS that can be applied in inductive setting.

COINS can effectively exploit unlabeled data to boost multi-label learning performance, and it is a general and flexible approach which can be combined with any existing multi-label learning algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following two questions: (1) How can the co-training framework be adapted to multi-label learning task to learn a multi-label classifier from labeled and unlabled data under inductive setting? (2) How can the pairwise ranking information on unlabeled data be exploited to refine the multi-label classifier?

the following questions: (i) How to design an inductive semi-supervised multi-class learning approach to learn from labeled and unlabled data? (ii) How to exploit unlabeled data to improve the performance on the test data?
the problem of learning a multi-label predictive model from a small number of labeled data and a large amount of unlabeled data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed COINS is a novel and effective semi-supervised inductive multi-label learning approach.
the paper proposes a new semi-supervised multi label learning method, and shows that it outperforms state-of-the-art approaches.
COINS is the best performing method in terms of accuracy and F-measure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
COINS is the first co-training-based semi-supervised multi- label learning approach that can generalize to unseen instances.
COINS is the first inductive semi-supervised multi-lable learning approach.
COINS is the first inductive approach to semi-supervised multi-class learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
co-training can be adapted for multi-label learning and it is effective in learning from labeled and/or unlabeled data.
co-training can be adapted to the inductive multi-label setting, and the proposed approach can be easily extended to other inductive multi-label learning algorithms.
co-training is a promising strategy for learning from both labeled and unlabeled instances in multi-label learning.
